figures.finding: American Samoa follows US federal labour law, and its minimum wages are set by industry, not by occupation, so a director employed there by a film or television employer falls under 'Miscellaneous Activities', USD 5.80 an hour from 30 September 2024. No directors' agreement or guild rate specific to the territory was found; whether the Fair Labor Standards Act's exemptions reach a salaried director was not checked.

figures.finding: The DGA's Basic Agreement reaches American Samoa: its section 17-201 applies it to work on motion pictures based in and performed in the United States, its territories and dependencies included, and the Department of the Interior holds American Samoa a US territory by deed of cession from 1900. The 2026 Memorandum of Agreement carries the 2023 agreement into the 2026 one (1 July 2026 to 30 June 2030) and leaves 17-201 as it was (its geographical part only reissues a bulletin and amends Sideletter No. 31), so a director there works on the DGA's terms, set as the US's are.

figures.applies: American Samoa, a director engaged by a DGA signatory, as the life's company is held to be in the US (the engine's reading: the life's company signs where a guild lets a producer sign). A non-signatory's director there has no guild terms; the game doesn't model one.

sources.said: The provisions of this BA shall apply to work on motion pictures based in the United States and performed in the United States (including its territories and dependencies) and Canada; provided, however, that the provisions of this BA shall also apply to work performed by any Employee employed by the Employer in the United States, to direct, or to be a UPM or an Assistant Director or Associate Director on a motion picture based outside the United States (including its territories and dependencies).

The terms of the 2023 BA (including all sideletters) shall be incorporated in the Directors Guild of America Basic Agreement of 2026, except as provided below and subject to conforming changes. … The term of the 2026 BA and the 2026 FLTTA shall be for four (4) years, commencing on July 1, 2026 to and including June 30, 2030. … 4. International Jurisdiction (U-4) A. Geographical Application (U-4.A.) … Modify Sideletter No. 31 to the Basic Agreement as follows:

territory An unincorporated United States insular area, of which there are currently thirteen, three in the Caribbean (Navassa Island, Puerto Rico and the United States Virgin Islands) and ten in the Pacific (American Samoa, Baker Island, Guam, Howland Island, Jarvis Island, Johnston Atoll, Kingman Reef, Midway Atoll, the Northern Mariana Islands and Wake Atoll).
American Samoa became a U.S. territory by deed of cession, starting in 1900.
